- Medium: The executed credit agreement, its five amendments, the indenture for the 2029 senior notes and four supplemental indentures were not supplied. The annual report lists them as exhibits filed elsewhere, and the run settings declare no legal documents. Maturities, pricing and the two maintenance covenants come from the debt notes and risk factors, which give no covenant definitions, baskets, release terms or redemption prices, and no source states a reported covenant ratio or the covenant earnings measure. Covenant headroom, security and priority conclusions need the executed documents or a compliance certificate. Basis: 10-K_2026-06-30_iivi-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 51, 105–108, 137–138 - Medium: No source states EBITDA or adjusted EBITDA. The releases reconcile non-GAAP operating income and earnings, and the cash flow statements give depreciation and amortization, so leverage and coverage have to be built from statement lines and cannot be tied to the issuer's or the lenders' definition. Basis: EX-99.1_2026-11-04_d176836dex991.htm.jsonl, pages 8–9; 10-K_2026-06-30_iivi-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 88 - Medium: Governance, ownership and customer detail is incomplete. Directors, compensation, beneficial ownership, related-party matters and director independence are incorporated by reference to a 2026 proxy statement that was not supplied, and the two customers that each contributed more than 10% of revenue are not named. The ownership picture rests on the notes, which name only the NVIDIA share purchase and the Silicon Carbide LLC partners. Basis: 10-K_2026-06-30_iivi-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 17, 28, 114, 116, 136–137 - Medium: Guarantor-level financial information was not found. The senior debt is guaranteed by certain subsidiaries, while the foreign unsecured facilities drawn since June 2026 are not guaranteed by the company or its other subsidiaries. No summarised guarantor and non-guarantor financials were supplied, so the split of earnings, cash and debt across those groups is not established. Basis: 10-K_2026-06-30_iivi-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 105, 107–108, 134; 10-Q_2026-09-30_iivi-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 11, 13–14 - Low: The first fiscal quarter of 2026 has no standalone quarterly report or release, the second fiscal quarter of 2026 has no release, and no balance sheet at 2025-09-30 or 2024-06-30 was supplied. Income and cash flow for the quarter ended 2025-09-30 appear as comparatives in the latest quarterly report, and its equity statement and cash reconciliation give some balances at that date, so four discrete quarters of fiscal 2026 can be rebuilt but not a full September 2025 balance sheet. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_iivi-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 3–5; 10-K_2026-06-30_iivi-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 85 - Low: The amount of letters of credit drawn on the revolving credit facility is not stated; the sources, searched for letters of credit, standby facilities and bank guarantees, give only the sub-limit. Availability is stated and the gap between the revolver commitment and that availability is not itemised, so liquidity net of letters of credit rests on the stated availability. Basis: 10-K_2026-06-30_iivi-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 78, 106–107; 10-Q_2026-09-30_iivi-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 12–13, 41; calculation X6 - Low: No credit rating, rating trigger, current price or yield, transaction terms, peer financial statements or portfolio data were supplied. The filings give period-end fair values for the notes and term loans from quoted prices at the last trading day before each period end, and the annual report names a peer group without peer financials. Ratings & triggers, Market-implied risk, Security selection and Peer benchmark would need those inputs. Basis: 10-K_2026-06-30_iivi-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 59, 132; 10-Q_2026-09-30_iivi-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 28 - Low: Forward information is limited to the outlook for the second quarter of fiscal 2027 and aims for later years; no multi-year projection or capital spending plan was found. Basis: EX-99.1_2026-11-04_d176836dex991.htm.jsonl, pages 2–3 - Low: Headline growth in the releases is stated on a pro forma basis, which no source defines or tabulates, so pro forma growth cannot be tied to reported revenue. facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: No controlling shareholder or sponsor is disclosed, and the one sponsor-style claim, the Series B convertible preferred stock, no longer exists. The two Series B issues carried an aggregate issue price of USD 2.15 billion. Their holder, who is not named in the filings, waived dividends from 2025-11-20, and all of the stock converted in the quarter ended 2025-12-31 into common shares equal to about 15.3% of the shares outstanding on 2026-11-02. That ended a claim ranking ahead of the common equity, on which dividends recognised were USD 123.69 million in fiscal 2025 and USD 31.75 million in fiscal 2026, with cash dividends of USD 11.44 million in each year. It also created a large common holding whose owner, current stake and selling intent are not established. The annual report's market-value calculation treats only directors and executive officers as affiliates, which fits a widely held company but does not prove that no large holder has influence. Basis: 10-K_2026-06-30_iivi-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 2, 59, 88, 114–115; 10-Q_2026-09-30_iivi-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 2; calculation C09; calculation C10

facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: NVIDIA is at once a shareholder, a customer and a capacity counterparty, which strengthens funding but ties Coherent's growth to one AI supply chain. On 2026-03-02 NVIDIA bought common stock for USD 2 billion at USD 256.80 a share, equal to 3.95% of shares outstanding on 2026-11-02 if all are still held. The six-month price-protection clause expired in September 2026 without being triggered, so no extra shares or cash were owed. Management states that the agreement is non-exclusive, includes a multi-billion-dollar purchase commitment with NVIDIA and future access and capacity rights for NVIDIA, and may require incremental investment in equipment, labour and working capital through 2030, with possible effects on revenue concentration, gross margin and capital expenditure. The filings do not say which party commits to buy, or the size, minimum volumes or term of the commitment, or whether NVIDIA is one of the two customers above 10% of revenue. Basis: 10-K_2026-06-30_iivi-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 60, 61, 79, 114; 10-Q_2026-09-30_iivi-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 19, 42; calculation C08

facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: The group is becoming a datacenter optics company with a shrinking industrial tail, so the diversification that once cushioned creditors is eroding. Datacenter & Communications was 55.90% of revenue in fiscal 2024, 64.63% in fiscal 2025, 74.10% in fiscal 2026 and 82.34% in the quarter to 2026-09-30. Its revenue grew 40.46% in fiscal 2026 and 79.06% in the latest quarter, while Industrial revenue fell 10.29% and 14.81%, mainly because of the two disposals. Quarterly segment revenue rose from USD 1,018.3 million in the quarter to 2025-06-30 to USD 1,951.7 million in the quarter to 2026-09-30, and the sequential increase widened from 7.04% to 20.85%, so any pause in AI datacenter orders would be sharper against a larger and faster-growing base. Capital expenditure was USD 1,102.91 million in fiscal 2026, 2.50x the prior year's, and USD 775.55 million in the latest quarter alone, in which the company also drew USD 785 million of new borrowings and realised USD 625 million from sales and maturities of short-term investments. facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: Part of the liquidity and part of the debt sit in subsidiaries where the parent's creditors have limited reach. Silicon Carbide LLC is owned about 75% by Coherent, with Denso and Mitsubishi Electric each holding about 12.5% after paying USD 1 billion in total in December 2023, and USD 581 million of restricted cash at 2026-09-30 can be used only by that subsidiary. facts.label: T2D.9 - Sponsor risk assessment
facts.text: The risk level is driven by the absence of any documented extraction, the conversion of the preferred stock and the USD 2 billion equity placement, because cash and equity stayed in the business and the equity base widened, which implies lower loss-given-default and refinancing risk for creditors on conduct alone. Countervailing evidence is the unnamed former preferred holder, the missing proxy statement and credit agreement text, the shift to subsidiary borrowing in the latest quarter, and an open export-control inquiry. The gate tests are met for issuer identity, issuer-specific behaviour, timing and funding source of each action; they are not met for holder identity, legal capacity, or related-party and fee disclosure, which are therefore held as gaps and not scored. facts.text: Liquidity is adequate and refinancing risk is back-ended, but the 2029 maturities carry a mechanism that forces action early. Cash and undrawn revolver availability were USD 2.22 billion at 2026-09-30, which covers about 2.56 quarters at the latest quarter's outflow, and scheduled principal was only USD 0.14 billion through fiscal 2029 but USD 2.14 billion in fiscal 2030 and USD 0.99 billion in fiscal 2031, together 95.83% of the total. The revolver and Term A fall due on 2030-09-26 unless a springing maturity applies 91 days before the Term B-3 loans and the 2029 notes mature, which happens if either is still outstanding and liquidity is below USD 250 million plus its principal, so refinancing those two instruments before 2029 also protects the revolver. facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: Business risk is concentrated, and the company itself says the demand may not prove sustainable. The datacenter and communications segment supplied 74.10% of fiscal 2026 revenue and 82.34% of the latest quarter, one customer took 20% of fiscal 2026 revenue and a second 12%. facts.label: Margin resilience
facts.text: Margins expanded sharply, but the company states that certain sales, research and overhead costs are relatively fixed, so operating leverage cuts both ways. facts.label: Competitive forces
facts.text: Competitive rivalry and technology change matter through pricing and share: the company says its markets change fast, alternatives can be more cost-effective, and large customers have bargained for concessions, so margin gains can erode. On an analyst reading, new entry is limited by the capital and process know-how that indium phosphide and laser manufacturing need, which protects margin, but the AI efficiency risk the company names could reduce compute and optical demand, and buyer power is high because a few customers dominate revenue. Supplier power is also real for sole and limited-source inputs and an industry-wide shortage of indium phosphide, which can cap output and raise cost. facts.text: Trade and regulatory factors are a material credit driver here. facts.label: Downside scenario
facts.text: The initiating condition is a delay or cut in orders from one or two large AI datacenter customers, or an efficiency shift that reduces optical demand, both named by the company as risks. The first operational break is underused new capacity and inventory that stops turning, with USD 3.34 billion of inventory, USD 11.8 billion of purchase commitments and USD 527.73 million of unpaid capital spending already in place. Revenue would fall below next-quarter guidance of USD 2.55 billion to USD 2.75 billion, gross margin would be at risk of falling below the 40% low end of guidance because costs are relatively fixed, and free cash flow would stay negative as capital spending is paid. Liquidity of USD 2.22 billion lasts about 2.56 quarters at the latest quarter's outflow, before undrawn foreign facilities, and if EBITDA fell back to its fiscal 2025 level net debt would be 2.15x EBITDA. Management levers are uncommitted capital spending, slower purchasing, drawing foreign lines, further equity of the kind NVIDIA provided, and selling the entity still held for sale. Whether resilience is sufficient to avoid liquidity distress is not established, because at the current outflow liquidity lasts under three quarters and avoiding distress would depend on management levers and market access that the filings do not evidence; observable triggers are a sequential fall in datacenter revenue, inventory growing faster than revenue, unpaid capital spending rising and foreign facility draws rising. facts.label: Overall credit view
facts.text: Overall, COHERENT CORP. presents an adequate business profile supported by scale, earnings growth and a larger equity base, but credit quality is constrained by negative free cash flow and concentration in one end market and a few customers. Cash-flow durability appears weak at present because capital spending and inventory absorb more than the business generates, although earnings and prepayments are rising. Refinancing capacity is likely to depend on earnings growth, on refinancing the Term B-3 loans and the 2029 notes before the springing test dates, and on continued access to subsidiary-level borrowing. The primary downside path is an AI order pause that strands inventory and commitments; the comparison with typical leveraged-credit issuers in the sector is not established because no peer data was supplied. Further analysis would require the credit agreement and its covenant definitions, the proxy statement, customer contract terms and a rating or market price. Fundamental credit review completed. Top risk: negative free cash flow while revenue is concentrated in one end market. ## Findings
### Bottom line

The sources are sufficient for a financial and fundamental credit snapshot of COHERENT CORP. through the quarter ended 2026-09-30, but not for covenant headroom, rating or relative-value conclusions, which would rest on documents the run does not hold. The audited annual report, three quarterly reports and three earnings releases all cover the issuer's own consolidated group, so no parent or sister-company statements are needed.

The executed credit agreement, its five amendments and the indenture are listed in the annual report's exhibit index but were not supplied, and no source states a covenant ratio, an EBITDA figure, a letter-of-credit balance or a credit rating. Governance and ownership detail sits in a proxy statement that was not supplied. Business & governance, Financial foundation and Fundamental credit can proceed with these limits written into their results.

## Gaps
Gaps are ranked Medium or Low by their effect on the three modules this run executes; none is High.

- Medium: The executed credit agreement, its five amendments, the indenture for the 2029 senior notes and four supplemental indentures were not supplied. The annual report lists them as exhibits filed elsewhere, and the run settings declare no legal documents. Maturities, pricing and the two maintenance covenants come from the debt notes and risk factors, which give no covenant definitions, baskets, release terms or redemption prices, and no source states a reported covenant ratio or the covenant earnings measure. Covenant headroom, security and priority conclusions need the executed documents or a compliance certificate.

- Medium: No source states EBITDA or adjusted EBITDA. The releases reconcile non-GAAP operating income and earnings, and the cash flow statements give depreciation and amortization, so leverage and coverage have to be built from statement lines and cannot be tied to the issuer's or the lenders' definition.

- Medium: Governance, ownership and customer detail is incomplete. Directors, compensation, beneficial ownership, related-party matters and director independence are incorporated by reference to a 2026 proxy statement that was not supplied, and the two customers that each contributed more than 10% of revenue are not named. The ownership picture rests on the notes, which name only the NVIDIA share purchase and the Silicon Carbide LLC partners.

- Medium: Guarantor-level financial information was not found. The senior debt is guaranteed by certain subsidiaries, while the foreign unsecured facilities drawn since June 2026 are not guaranteed by the company or its other subsidiaries. No summarised guarantor and non-guarantor financials were supplied, so the split of earnings, cash and debt across those groups is not established.

- Low: The first fiscal quarter of 2026 has no standalone quarterly report or release, the second fiscal quarter of 2026 has no release, and no balance sheet at 2025-09-30 or 2024-06-30 was supplied. Income and cash flow for the quarter ended 2025-09-30 appear as comparatives in the latest quarterly report, and its equity statement and cash reconciliation give some balances at that date, so four discrete quarters of fiscal 2026 can be rebuilt but not a full September 2025 balance sheet.

- Low: The amount of letters of credit drawn on the revolving credit facility is not stated; the sources, searched for letters of credit, standby facilities and bank guarantees, give only the sub-limit. Availability is stated and the gap between the revolver commitment and that availability is not itemised, so liquidity net of letters of credit rests on the stated availability.
Basis: 10-K_2026-06-30_iivi-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 78, 106–107; 10-Q_2026-09-30_iivi-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 12–13, 41; calculation X6

- Low: No credit rating, rating trigger, current price or yield, transaction terms, peer financial statements or portfolio data were supplied. The filings give period-end fair values for the notes and term loans from quoted prices at the last trading day before each period end, and the annual report names a peer group without peer financials. Ratings & triggers, Market-implied risk, Security selection and Peer benchmark would need those inputs.

- Low: Forward information is limited to the outlook for the second quarter of fiscal 2027 and aims for later years; no multi-year projection or capital spending plan was found. Forward credit model and Downside work would rest on assumptions the user has not entered.
Basis: EX-99.1_2026-11-04_d176836dex991.htm.jsonl, pages 2–3
- Low: Headline growth in the releases is stated on a pro forma basis, which no source defines or tabulates, so pro forma growth cannot be tied to reported revenue.

- Low: The August 2026 facility is sized at about USD 945 million in the annual report, which ties the amount to exchange rates at signing, and at about USD 950 million in the latest quarterly report. Both are kept, each at its own report date; the later report states first use on 2026-08-17 and USD 598 million drawn at 2026-09-30, and no source says why the stated sizes differ.
Basis: 10-K_2026-06-30_iivi-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 78, 134; 10-Q_2026-09-30_iivi-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 14, 41; calculation X8

- Low: The latest quarterly report's management discussion attributes the USD 773 million of other-facility borrowing to the first quarter of fiscal 2026, while its cash flow statement shows the borrowing in the three months ended 2026-09-30 and none in the year-earlier column. The statement and the period headings govern, so the borrowing belongs to the first quarter of fiscal 2027.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_iivi-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 4, 40

- Low: The annual report's debt note describes the original 2022 terms, with a USD 350 million revolver and a term loan A maturing in 2027, beside the September 2025 amendments, which replaced them with a USD 700 million revolver and a term loan A maturing in 2030 unless the springing maturity applies. The amended terms and the 2026-06-30 debt table control.

## Findings
### Bottom line

Leverage fell to 2.07x total debt and 1.32x net debt over EBITDA in fiscal 2026, but free cash flow was negative and debt rose in the latest quarter, so creditors depend on EBITDA growth, not cash generation, to hold leverage down. The EBITDA is derived from statement lines because the issuer states none, and it includes net one-off gains of USD 70.34 million.

### Financial interpretation

The leverage fall in fiscal 2026 came from earnings and equity, not from operating cash. Derived EBITDA grew by 75.07% to USD 1.56 billion while total debt fell by USD 0.46 billion: the issuer made USD 509 million of term loan payments, USD 502 million of them voluntary, while raising USD 2.00 billion from a placement of common shares. Leverage was 4.14x total debt and 3.12x net debt in fiscal 2025. In the quarter to 2026-09-30 total debt rose by USD 0.78 billion to USD 4.00 billion as foreign facilities were drawn, so leverage on last-twelve-months EBITDA was 2.33x total debt and 1.43x net debt.
Basis: 10-K_2026-06-30_iivi-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 78, 88–89, 104; 10-Q_2026-09-30_iivi-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 3–5, 10; calculation C01; calculation C03; calculation C04

Interest cover improved to 8.24x in fiscal 2026 from 3.47x because derived EBITDA rose while cash interest paid fell from USD 256.70 million to USD 189.26 million; on the twelve months to 2026-09-30 it was 9.65x. After capital spending the cover is lower, 2.41x in fiscal 2026, which shows how much of the earnings the build-out absorbs before tax and working capital.
Basis: 10-K_2026-06-30_iivi-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 88–89; 10-Q_2026-09-30_iivi-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 4–5; calculation C03; calculation C04

Cash conversion did not follow earnings. Operating cash flow was USD 79.51 million in fiscal 2026 against derived EBITDA of USD 1.56 billion because inventories absorbed USD 1.18 billion, only partly offset by a USD 0.75 billion rise in payables, and capital spending of USD 1.10 billion left free cash flow at negative USD 1.02 billion. The latest quarter repeated the pattern: operating cash flow of negative USD 92.68 million and capital spending of USD 775.55 million gave free cash flow of negative USD 0.87 billion, with a further USD 527.73 million of capital spending unpaid in accounts payable at 2026-09-30.
Basis: 10-K_2026-06-30_iivi-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 88–89; 10-Q_2026-09-30_iivi-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 4–5; calculation C04; calculation C06

Liquidity at 2026-09-30 was cash of USD 1.55 billion, short-term investments of USD 0.20 billion and revolver availability of USD 0.67 billion, against scheduled principal of only USD 0.14 billion through fiscal 2029 but USD 2.14 billion in fiscal 2030 and USD 0.99 billion in fiscal 2031 on the schedule at 2026-06-30, before the USD 0.80 billion of foreign facilities drawn since, which mature in 2029. The revolver and Term A fall due on 2030-09-26 unless a springing maturity applies 91 days before the stated maturity of the senior notes or Term B loans if they remain outstanding and liquidity is below USD 250 million plus their principal, so refinancing those two instruments before 2029 matters to the revolver as well.
Basis: 10-K_2026-06-30_iivi-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 104, 106–107; 10-Q_2026-09-30_iivi-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 10–12, 41; calculation C05; calculation C13

Part of the funding is non-debt. Accounts payable rose from USD 0.85 billion at 2025-06-30 to USD 2.51 billion at 2026-09-30, customer advances added USD 269.28 million of cash in the latest quarter, and supplier-finance arrangements covered USD 27 million of payables at 2026-06-30. These fund inventory and capital spending without appearing as debt, so they reverse if suppliers shorten terms or customers stop prepaying, and they make the debt-based leverage figures understate the call on cash.

The derived EBITDA is a statement-based estimate, not an issuer or covenant measure: the fiscal 2026 figure includes USD 198.13 million of gains from the sale of a business and an equity investment and USD 127.79 million of impairment and restructuring charges. The credit agreement sets a maximum total net leverage of 4.25x and a minimum interest coverage of 2.50x, but no covenant ratio or definition was supplied, so headroom is not established. The August 2026 facility is sized at USD 945 million in the annual report and USD 950 million in the latest quarterly report, with USD 598 million drawn at 2026-09-30; both are kept at their own dates.
Basis: 10-K_2026-06-30_iivi-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 51, 78, 134; 10-Q_2026-09-30_iivi-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 14, 41; calculation C10; calculation C12

The strongest contrary evidence is the earnings trajectory: management's outlook puts second-quarter revenue between USD 2.55 billion and USD 2.75 billion against USD 2.37 billion in the latest quarter, and the inventory build can turn back into cash if demand holds. That view wins if operating cash flow turns positive and the drawn foreign facilities stop rising; it loses if capital spending now held in payables falls due before inventory converts. Operating cash flow, the payables balance and the foreign facility balance are the observable tests.

## Gaps

- Medium: The issuer states no EBITDA, adjusted EBITDA or covenant earnings measure, so leverage and cover use EBITDA derived from statement lines. The fiscal 2026 figure keeps USD 198.13 million of gains and USD 127.79 million of charges, and the issuer's non-GAAP operating income is a different measure, so the ratios cannot be compared with lender definitions. A compliance certificate or the credit agreement definitions would close the gap.
Basis: 10-K_2026-06-30_iivi-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 86, 88–89; EX-99.1_2026-11-04_d176836dex991.htm.jsonl, page 8; calculation C03; calculation C10

- Medium: The balance sheets at 2025-09-30 and 2024-06-30 were not supplied, and the quarter-end balance sheets at 2025-12-31 and 2026-03-31 were not built into the statement tables, so leverage is stated at 2025-06-30, 2026-06-30 and 2026-09-30 only. The quarterly debt tables in the second and third quarterly reports would close the interim gap; the earlier dates need the prior filings.

- Medium: The amount of letters of credit drawn on the revolving credit facility is not stated, so undrawn committed facilities use the availability the issuer states and may include letters of credit already issued. The gap between the commitment and stated availability is not itemised.

- Medium: Debt by seniority is incomplete. The credit facilities are described as senior secured and the notes as unsecured, but the security, guarantees and rank of the foreign facilities, the local lines and the Germany loan are not stated, and no guarantor-level financial statements were supplied. The debt stack therefore shows the secured facilities and the notes only, and senior secured debt is not calculated as a total.

- Low: Source dashes are kept as missing values, not zero: fiscal 2025 and 2024 gains on sale of a business, fiscal 2024 impairment of assets held for sale, fiscal 2024 and 2025 gains on sale of an equity investment, first-quarter fiscal 2027 impairment, gain and preferred dividends, and several cash flow lines. Reported totals and the statement identities hold, so the missing lines do not break any total.

- Low: Capital expenditure is not split between maintenance and growth, and capital expenditure held in accounts payable is outside the cash figure, so recurring free cash flow and the cash still to be paid are not established beyond the amount stated for the latest quarter.

- Low: Interest income is named as a component of other income, net but not stated as an amount for fiscal 2026, so net interest expense is not established. Pension underfunding of USD 49 million at 2026-06-30 is stated by plan in whole millions and kept outside debt.
Basis: 10-K_2026-06-30_iivi-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 69, 86, 110–111; calculation C15

- Low: Segment composition changed on 2026-07-01 and prior periods were not recast, so first-quarter fiscal 2027 segment figures do not compare cleanly with the year-earlier quarter. The issuer says the effect is not material and does not give the amounts moved.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_iivi-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 25

- Low: Headline growth in the releases is stated on a pro forma basis that no source defines, so only reported growth is used. The latest quarterly report also places the USD 773 million of other-facility borrowing in the first quarter of fiscal 2026 in its text, while the statement shows it in the quarter to 2026-09-30; the statement governs.

spans.text: ## Request

Business and governance review for COHERENT CORP. (cohr) as of 2026-11-05 under the credit snapshot pathway. Scope: business and operating model, revenue mix, ownership and control, capital allocation and sponsor behaviour, transactions and new debt, and issuer history, drawn from the seven issuer documents and the source readiness analysis. It states no valuation, rating, covenant-capacity or recovery conclusion.
## Sources

No external sources were used. Document dates are the signature dates the documents state; the filing dates are not stated.
## Findings
### Bottom line

Creditors face operating concentration risk, not owner-behaviour risk: no controlling holder is disclosed and no common dividend or buyback took cash out, but earnings depend on AI datacenter demand and two unnamed customers. The Datacenter & Communications segment supplied 74.10% of fiscal 2026 revenue and 82.34% of the latest quarter, and one customer alone took 20% of fiscal 2026 revenue.
Basis: 10-K_2026-06-30_iivi-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 128–129; 10-Q_2026-09-30_iivi-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 25; calculation C01

Governance and sponsor risk is low on conduct visible in the filings: the preferred stock converted into common, NVIDIA added USD 2 billion of equity and no shares were repurchased. That rating is provisional because the proxy statement, board data and holder-level ownership were not supplied.
### Key findings

No controlling shareholder or sponsor is disclosed, and the one sponsor-style claim, the Series B convertible preferred stock, no longer exists. The two Series B issues carried an aggregate issue price of USD 2.15 billion. Their holder, who is not named in the filings, waived dividends from 2025-11-20, and all of the stock converted in the quarter ended 2025-12-31 into common shares equal to about 15.3% of the shares outstanding on 2026-11-02. That ended a claim ranking ahead of the common equity, on which dividends recognised were USD 123.69 million in fiscal 2025 and USD 31.75 million in fiscal 2026, with cash dividends of USD 11.44 million in each year. It also created a large common holding whose owner, current stake and selling intent are not established. The annual report's market-value calculation treats only directors and executive officers as affiliates, which fits a widely held company but does not prove that no large holder has influence.
Basis: 10-K_2026-06-30_iivi-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 2, 59, 88, 114–115; 10-Q_2026-09-30_iivi-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 2; calculation C09; calculation C10

NVIDIA is at once a shareholder, a customer and a capacity counterparty, which strengthens funding but ties Coherent's growth to one AI supply chain. On 2026-03-02 NVIDIA bought common stock for USD 2 billion at USD 256.80 a share, equal to 3.95% of shares outstanding on 2026-11-02 if all are still held. The six-month price-protection clause expired in September 2026 without being triggered, so no extra shares or cash were owed. Management states that the agreement is non-exclusive, includes a multi-billion-dollar purchase commitment with NVIDIA and future access and capacity rights for NVIDIA, and may require incremental investment in equipment, labour and working capital through 2030, with possible effects on revenue concentration, gross margin and capital expenditure. The filings do not say which party commits to buy, or the size, minimum volumes or term of the commitment, or whether NVIDIA is one of the two customers above 10% of revenue.
Basis: 10-K_2026-06-30_iivi-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 60, 61, 79, 114; 10-Q_2026-09-30_iivi-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 19, 42; calculation C08

The group is becoming a datacenter optics company with a shrinking industrial tail, so the diversification that once cushioned creditors is eroding. Datacenter & Communications was 55.90% of revenue in fiscal 2024, 64.63% in fiscal 2025, 74.10% in fiscal 2026 and 82.34% in the quarter to 2026-09-30. Its revenue grew 40.46% in fiscal 2026 and 79.06% in the latest quarter, while Industrial revenue fell 10.29% and 14.81%, mainly because of the two disposals. Quarterly segment revenue rose from USD 1,018.3 million in the quarter to 2025-06-30 to USD 1,951.7 million in the quarter to 2026-09-30, and the sequential increase widened from 7.04% to 20.85%, so any pause in AI datacenter orders would be sharper against a larger and faster-growing base.

Basis: 10-K_2026-06-30_iivi-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 128; 10-Q_2026-09-30_iivi-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 25, 38–39; EX-99.1_2026-08-12_d128030dex991.htm.jsonl, pages 7–8; EX-99.1_2026-11-04_d176836dex991.htm.jsonl, page 7; calculation C01; calculation C03; calculation C04

Customer concentration is high, rising and unattributed. One customer took 20% of fiscal 2026 revenue after 10% in each of the two prior years, and a second took 12%, together about 32%, mostly in the Datacenter & Communications segment. The customers are not named, the issuer warns that losing, cancelling or delaying their orders could harm the business, and customer prepayments are small at USD 63 million of contract liabilities, so there is no advance-payment cushion if orders slow.
Basis: 10-K_2026-06-30_iivi-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 17, 28, 101, 129; calculation C13

Growth is absorbing cash faster than the business generates it, so debt and equity funding, not operations, are paying for the build-out. Operating cash flow fell to USD 79.51 million in fiscal 2026 from USD 633.60 million because the company built inventory, which rose 79.53% to 2026-06-30 and a further 29.46% in the next quarter to USD 3.34 billion. Capital expenditure was USD 1,102.91 million in fiscal 2026, 2.50x the prior year's, and USD 775.55 million in the latest quarter alone, in which the company also drew USD 785 million of new borrowings and realised USD 625 million from sales and maturities of short-term investments. Vendor purchase commitments stood at USD 11.8 billion at 2026-06-30, so leverage depends on earnings growth continuing while commitments run ahead of revenue.
Basis: 10-K_2026-06-30_iivi-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 76, 85, 88, 113; 10-Q_2026-09-30_iivi-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 2, 4, 39; calculation C11

A large non-cash exposure sits in the shrinking Industrial segment, which holds 73.71% of the USD 4.38 billion of goodwill but supplied only 25.90% of fiscal 2026 revenue and 17.66% of the latest quarter. The segment lost revenue to the sale of the aerospace and defense business for about USD 400 million and of the Munich division at a loss of USD 96 million, and one more entity is still held for sale. The auditor's critical audit matter is the goodwill of the Lasers reporting unit, USD 3.1 billion, whose fair value depends on forecast revenue and the discount rate, and the filings do not state how that unit maps to the two segments. An impairment would not use cash but would cut equity and, where a lender definition starts from reported earnings, could matter; those definitions were not supplied.
Basis: 10-K_2026-06-30_iivi-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 83, 101, 103, 128; 10-Q_2026-09-30_iivi-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 25, 34; calculation C07; calculation C01

Part of the liquidity and part of the debt sit in subsidiaries where the parent's creditors have limited reach. Silicon Carbide LLC is owned about 75% by Coherent, with Denso and Mitsubishi Electric each holding about 12.5% after paying USD 1 billion in total in December 2023, and USD 581 million of restricted cash at 2026-09-30 can be used only by that subsidiary. Separately, foreign subsidiaries had USD 803 million outstanding under local credit lines and the August 2026 facility, equal to 20.07% of total debt obligations, and neither the parent nor any other subsidiary guarantees them, so those lenders' recourse is to the borrowers. The filings do not state the borrowers' assets, whether they guarantee the secured credit facilities, or the minority holders' rights in Silicon Carbide LLC.
Basis: 10-K_2026-06-30_iivi-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 116; 10-Q_2026-09-30_iivi-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 14, 41–42; calculation C12; calculation C14

Capital allocation shows no extraction. The company repurchased no shares in fiscal 2026 and has no repurchase programme, has not historically paid a cash dividend on its common stock, and paid USD 509 million on its term facilities in fiscal 2026, of which USD 502 million was voluntary. Cash costs of equity compensation are rising, with payments for employees' minimum tax obligations up 43.39% in fiscal 2026 to USD 77.42 million and at USD 129 million in the latest quarter, 3.49x the same quarter a year earlier. An export-control inquiry into past sales to Huawei has no estimated loss, and the company states it was in compliance with its credit agreement and indenture covenants at 2026-06-30 and 2026-09-30.
### Contrary evidence and what would change the view

The strongest evidence against a concentration-led view is that the concentration is with some of the most capable buyers in the market and is becoming contractual: NVIDIA invested USD 2 billion and signed a multi-year supply agreement with a multi-billion-dollar purchase commitment, the Datacenter & Communications segment earned a profit margin of 25.21% in fiscal 2026 against 19.00% two years earlier, and shareholders' equity rose from USD 5.64 billion to USD 10.90 billion, a much larger buffer beneath the debt. The strongest evidence against a low governance reading is what is missing: the proxy statement, the board's composition and the owner of the shares issued when the preferred stock converted.
Basis: 10-K_2026-06-30_iivi-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 60, 61, 86, 114, 128; calculation C02

The view would worsen if customer disclosure showed that the 20% customer and the NVIDIA commitment are one counterparty on short or cancellable terms, if revenue fell below management's second-quarter outlook of USD 2.55 billion to USD 2.75 billion, if capital expenditure kept outrunning operating cash flow after the quarter to 2026-09-30, if the export-control inquiry ended in a material penalty, or if the proxy statement or credit agreement showed a holder with board rights or capacity for large distributions. It would improve if the largest customers were named with minimum purchase terms, if operating cash flow turned positive after capital expenditure while inventory stopped rising, and if the former preferred holder were shown to have sold its shares without conflict.
### Limitations

- The proxy statement was not supplied, so board composition, director independence, executive pay, holder-level ownership and related-party dealings are not established; the low governance and sponsor rating would change if they showed a controlling holder, board rights for NVIDIA or the former preferred holder, or fee arrangements.
Basis: 10-K_2026-06-30_iivi-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 3, 136

- The former Series B holder is not named and its holding after conversion is not stated, so the finding that no controlling holder is disclosed cannot exclude that this holder owns a stake of about 15.3% of shares outstanding with influence over the board or over sales into the market.
Basis: 10-K_2026-06-30_iivi-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 114–115; 10-Q_2026-09-30_iivi-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 2; calculation C09

- The credit agreement and indenture text were not supplied, so the capacity to pay dividends, repurchase shares, add subsidiary debt or release guarantees is not established; the sponsor conclusion rests on behaviour, not on legal capacity.

- The customers above 10% of revenue are unnamed and the purchase commitment with NVIDIA is neither sized nor assigned to a party, so the concentration findings give the shares but not the counterparty, the contract term or the minimum volumes that would show how much revenue is committed.
Basis: 10-K_2026-06-30_iivi-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 61, 129

- Segment disclosure splits revenue between Datacenter & Communications and Industrial only, with no separate datacenter and communications revenue and no volume, price, backlog or order data, so growth cannot be divided between price and volume and revenue visibility beyond the next-quarter outlook cannot be measured.
- The export-control inquiry has no determination and no stated loss range, so the regulatory-conduct element of the governance assessment is held open rather than scored.

### Transaction summary and new debt issues

NVIDIA bought 7,788,161 newly issued common shares at USD 256.80 a share on 2026-03-02 for USD 2 billion gross, a private placement the issuer says will fund research, capacity and operations. The shares carried a six-month lock-up and a six-month price-protection clause, which expired in September 2026 without being triggered. A separate multi-year, non-exclusive agreement includes a multi-billion-dollar purchase commitment with NVIDIA, without saying which party commits, and capacity rights for NVIDIA, and the issuer says it may require Coherent to invest in equipment, labour and working capital through 2030.
Basis: 10-K_2026-06-30_iivi-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 60, 61, 79, 114; 10-Q_2026-09-30_iivi-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 19, 42; calculation C08

Series B-1, issued in March 2021 for USD 750 million, and Series B-2, issued on 2022-07-01 for USD 1.4 billion, converted into 30.1 million common shares during the quarter ended 2025-12-31 at a conversion price of USD 85 a share, most by the holder's election and the rest by the company's. The holder waived dividends from 2025-11-20, no Series B stock remained at 2026-06-30 or 2026-09-30, and USD 2.5 billion moved from mezzanine equity to common equity.
Basis: 10-K_2026-06-30_iivi-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 114–115; 10-Q_2026-09-30_iivi-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 19; calculation C09; calculation C10

The aerospace and defense business was sold on 2025-09-02 for about USD 400 million with a gain of USD 115 million, and the Munich, Germany materials-processing tools division was sold on 2026-01-30 at a loss of USD 96 million, largely taken earlier as impairment charges. One further entity classified as held for sale in the fourth quarter of fiscal 2026 was still held for sale at 2026-09-30, so a third disposal is possible but no agreement is stated.

On 2025-09-26 the Credit Agreement was amended twice. Amendment No. 4 replaced the revolver with USD 700 million of senior secured commitments, added a USD 1,250 million senior secured Term A tranche whose proceeds repaid the existing Term A loans, and set both to mature on the earlier of 2030-09-26 and a springing maturity 91 days before the 2029 notes or term B loans if liquidity is below USD 250 million plus the principal still outstanding. Amendment No. 5 replaced the term B loans with Term B-3 loans at a SOFR-based rate with a 0.50% floor plus 1.75%, maturing on 2029-07-01. The facilities are guaranteed by the borrower and certain subsidiaries and secured on substantially all their assets, and no revolver borrowings were outstanding at 2026-09-30.

In June, July and August 2026 two foreign subsidiaries signed unsecured credit lines of up to USD 475 million that mature in 2029 and had USD 205 million outstanding at 2026-09-30. On 2026-08-12 another foreign subsidiary signed the August 2026 Facility with local lenders, first used on 2026-08-17 and drawn at USD 598 million at 2026-09-30, at three-month Term SOFR plus 20 basis points for US dollar loans, to fund working capital and repay intercompany loans. The annual report states its commitments as approximately USD 945 million and the quarterly report as approximately USD 950 million, a difference the filings do not reconcile. Neither the parent nor any other subsidiary guarantees these facilities, so on an analyst reading their lenders have first call on the borrowers' own assets and cash flow; the filings do not state those assets.
Basis: 10-K_2026-06-30_iivi-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 78, 134; 10-Q_2026-09-30_iivi-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 14, 41; calculation C12
The filings disclose no new bond or term loan issue other than the Term A tranche above and the foreign facilities; the only notes outstanding are the 2029 senior notes issued in December 2021.

Sponsor / Governance Risk Level: Low.

The risk level is driven by the absence of any documented extraction, the conversion of the preferred stock and the USD 2 billion equity placement, because cash and equity stayed in the business and the equity base widened, which implies lower loss-given-default and refinancing risk for creditors on conduct alone. Countervailing evidence is the unnamed former preferred holder, the missing proxy statement and credit agreement text, the shift to subsidiary borrowing in the latest quarter, and an open export-control inquiry. The gate tests are met for issuer identity, issuer-specific behaviour, timing and funding source of each action; they are not met for holder identity, legal capacity, or related-party and fee disclosure, which are therefore held as gaps and not scored. Governance review completed with limitations. Key gaps: proxy statement, holder identity, credit agreement text.

## Gaps

- Medium: The 2026 proxy statement was not supplied, so director independence and committees, executive pay, holder-level ownership and related-party dealings are not established. The governance and sponsor assessment rests on conduct visible in the filings and stays provisional until the proxy statement is read.

- Medium: The former Series B holder is not named, and neither its current holding nor any board or investor rights are stated. The shares issued on conversion equal about 15.3% of shares outstanding, so a large unnamed holder could influence the board or sell into the market; beneficial-ownership filings would close the gap.
Basis: 10-K_2026-06-30_iivi-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 114–115; 10-Q_2026-09-30_iivi-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 2; calculation C09

- Medium: The customers above 10% of revenue are not named and the purchase commitment with NVIDIA is described only as multi-billion-dollar, so the committing party, term and minimum volumes behind the 20% and 12% customer shares are not established. Customer disclosure or the agreement terms would close the gap.
Basis: 10-K_2026-06-30_iivi-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 61, 129; calculation C13

- Medium: The credit agreement, the indenture and any compliance certificates were not supplied, so the capacity to pay dividends, repurchase shares, add subsidiary debt or release guarantees is not established, and the conduct assessment cannot be tested against what the documents permit.

- Medium: The investment the NVIDIA capacity agreement may require through 2030 is not quantified, so the future funding need behind the capital expenditure ramp cannot be sized beyond the USD 11.8 billion of purchase commitments already stated.

- Low: Silicon Carbide LLC minority rights, distribution rules and separate results are not supplied, so how much of the USD 581 million of restricted cash and of the subsidiary's value is reachable by group creditors is not established.
- Low: The export-control inquiry has no determination and no stated loss range, so any penalty or remedial cost cannot be sized.

- Low: The issuer gives no split of datacenter and communications revenue and no backlog, order intake, price or volume data, so growth quality and revenue visibility beyond the next quarter cannot be measured.

- Low: The annual report states the August 2026 Facility commitments as about USD 945 million and the latest quarterly report as about USD 950 million; the filings do not reconcile the difference and the facility size is not used in any ratio here.

Fundamental credit synthesis for COHERENT CORP. (cohr) as of 2026-11-05 under the credit snapshot pathway. Scope: business and financial profile, strengths and weaknesses, outlook, downside path, materiality ranking and monitoring triggers, built on the supplied analyses and the issuer documents. It gives no rating, security recommendation, legal-capacity conclusion or sizing.

## Findings
### Bottom line

Coherent's credit profile is strong on scale, earnings growth and equity but weak on cash conversion, so creditors rely on earnings growth and outside funding, not free cash flow, and are exposed if AI datacenter demand pauses before the build-out pays back. Total debt was 2.07x derived EBITDA of USD 1.56 billion in fiscal 2026, yet free cash flow was negative USD 1.02 billion and capital spending over the last twelve months, USD 1.77 billion, exceeded EBITDA.
Basis: 10-K_2026-06-30_iivi-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 88–89; 10-Q_2026-09-30_iivi-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 4; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C01; calculation C04; calculation C06

Refinancing risk is low until 2029, after which USD 2.14 billion falls due in fiscal 2030, and liquidity of USD 2.22 billion would cover about 2.56 quarters at the latest quarter's free cash outflow. Governance and sponsor risk is low.

Basis: 10-K_2026-06-30_iivi-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 104; 10-Q_2026-09-30_iivi-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 2, 13, 41; Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C07; calculation C08
### Key findings

The strongest support is earnings power at scale, and it holds once one-offs are removed. Revenue grew 22.51% to USD 7.12 billion in fiscal 2026 and 49.89% in the latest quarter, the datacenter segment earned a profit margin of 25.21%, and EBITDA excluding gains and charges rose from 15.46% of revenue in fiscal 2024 to 20.93% in fiscal 2026 and 23.66% in the latest quarter. Management's outlook is revenue of USD 2.55 billion to USD 2.75 billion for the next quarter and a target of USD 3 billion of revenue in a quarter by the end of fiscal 2027; these are management targets, not reported results.

Basis: 10-K_2026-06-30_iivi-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 128; 10-Q_2026-09-30_iivi-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 25; EX-99.1_2026-11-04_d176836dex991.htm.jsonl, pages 2–3; Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C02; calculation C03; calculation C12

Reported EBITDA growth overstates the improvement. Derived EBITDA grew 75.07% in fiscal 2026, but excluding gains and charges the growth was 31.11%, because fiscal 2025 carried USD 245.07 million of impairment and restructuring charges and fiscal 2026 carried USD 198.13 million of disposal gains. On that stricter basis total debt was 2.16x EBITDA in fiscal 2026 and 2.29x over the last twelve months, against 2.07x and 2.33x on the derived basis, so the leverage conclusion holds but the growth rate should be read as about one third, not three quarters.
Basis: 10-K_2026-06-30_iivi-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 86, 88; 10-Q_2026-09-30_iivi-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 3–4; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C01; calculation C02; calculation C04

Free cash flow is the weakest dimension, and outside capital rather than operations is funding the build-out. Operating cash flow was USD 79.51 million in fiscal 2026 because inventories absorbed USD 1.18 billion, only partly offset by a USD 0.75 billion rise in payables, and capital spending of USD 1.10 billion left free cash flow at negative USD 1.02 billion. The latest quarter was worse at negative USD 868.23 million, with USD 527.73 million of further capital spending unpaid in payables at 2026-09-30 and inventories at USD 3.34 billion. Over the last twelve months capital spending of USD 1.77 billion equalled 101.64% of EBITDA excluding gains and charges, so the build-out absorbs all of the earnings before interest, tax and working capital, and vendor purchase commitments of USD 11.8 billion extend the obligation beyond the capital budget.
Basis: 10-K_2026-06-30_iivi-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 88, 113; 10-Q_2026-09-30_iivi-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 2, 4, 5; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C06

Liquidity is adequate and refinancing risk is back-ended, but the 2029 maturities carry a mechanism that forces action early. Cash and undrawn revolver availability were USD 2.22 billion at 2026-09-30, which covers about 2.56 quarters at the latest quarter's outflow, and scheduled principal was only USD 0.14 billion through fiscal 2029 but USD 2.14 billion in fiscal 2030 and USD 0.99 billion in fiscal 2031, together 95.83% of the total. The revolver and Term A fall due on 2030-09-26 unless a springing maturity applies 91 days before the Term B-3 loans and the 2029 notes mature, which happens if either is still outstanding and liquidity is below USD 250 million plus its principal, so refinancing those two instruments before 2029 also protects the revolver. Foreign facilities of USD 803 million that the parent does not guarantee add subsidiary-level debt, and no rating or market price was supplied, so market access is not tested.

Basis: 10-K_2026-06-30_iivi-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 104, 105–107; 10-Q_2026-09-30_iivi-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 2, 10, 13, 14, 41; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C07; calculation C08; calculation C09

Business risk is concentrated, and the company itself says the demand may not prove sustainable. The datacenter and communications segment supplied 74.10% of fiscal 2026 revenue and 82.34% of the latest quarter, one customer took 20% of fiscal 2026 revenue and a second 12%. Management warns that the recent AI-driven demand may not be sustainable, that large customers can cancel or delay orders, that some suppliers require noncancellable commitments or advance payments, and that because certain sales, research and overhead costs are relatively fixed, lower demand would cut gross margin and operating income, so a pause would hit earnings harder than revenue.
Basis: 10-K_2026-06-30_iivi-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 27–29, 128, 129; 10-Q_2026-09-30_iivi-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 25; Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C12

Financial policy supports creditors but is shifting toward debt. There were no repurchases and no common dividend, shareholders' equity rose from USD 5.64 billion to USD 10.90 billion after the preferred stock converted and NVIDIA invested USD 2 billion, and Business & governance rates governance and sponsor risk low on conduct. In the quarter to 2026-09-30, however, total debt rose from USD 3.22 billion to USD 4.00 billion as foreign subsidiaries drew facilities, and that rating stays provisional until the proxy statement and credit agreement text are read.

### Contrary evidence and what would change the view

The strongest evidence against the weak cash-conversion reading is that the build-out looks contracted rather than speculative. Customer prepayments added USD 269.28 million in the latest quarter and contract liabilities were USD 333 million at 2026-09-30 against USD 63 million at 2026-06-30, which corrects the year-end reading in Business & governance that prepayments were small. NVIDIA invested USD 2 billion and signed a multi-year agreement that includes a multi-billion-dollar purchase commitment, management guides next-quarter revenue to USD 2.55 billion to USD 2.75 billion, and inventories of USD 3.34 billion turn into cash if that revenue arrives. Net debt was 1.43x last-twelve-months derived EBITDA, so leverage is not yet the binding constraint.

### Limitations

- No credit rating, bond price or spread was supplied, so the refinancing-capacity conclusion rests on maturity profile, liquidity and leverage alone; a rating or trading level could move it in either direction.

- The outlook is one quarter of revenue guidance plus management targets, with no multi-year forecast or order data, so the outlook and downside conclusions are qualitative and the arithmetic illustrations are not forecasts.
Basis: EX-99.1_2026-11-04_d176836dex991.htm.jsonl, pages 2–3

- The company gives no split of fixed and variable costs, so the margin-resilience conclusion relies on its statement that certain sales, research and overhead costs are relatively fixed and on segment margin history, not on a measured drop-through.
Basis: 10-K_2026-06-30_iivi-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 28, 128

- The cancellable share of the USD 11.8 billion of purchase commitments, the supplier prepayments and the inventory reserves are not stated, so the size of a downside write-down or cash call cannot be established.
Basis: 10-K_2026-06-30_iivi-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 28, 113

- EBITDA excluding gains and charges is an analyst adjustment that removes only identified disposal gains and impairment and restructuring charges, so the leverage and growth conclusions carry that judgement and recurring integration costs, share-based pay and other items stay in.
Basis: calculation C01
- No peer or sector data was supplied, so the strong readings of scale and margins are judged against the company's own history, not against comparable issuers.
### Strengths and weaknesses

Earnings power at scale is the first credit strength. Revenue of USD 7.12 billion grew 22.51% in fiscal 2026, the datacenter segment earned a profit margin of 25.21%, and EBITDA excluding gains and charges moved from 15.46% of revenue in fiscal 2024 to 20.93% in fiscal 2026 as volume outran costs that the company says are partly fixed. That lifts debt service capacity: derived EBITDA covered cash interest 8.24x in fiscal 2026 and 9.65x over the last twelve months.

Basis: 10-K_2026-06-30_iivi-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 128, 86–89; 10-Q_2026-09-30_iivi-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 3–4; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C02; calculation C03; calculation C05; calculation C12

A larger equity base and conservative shareholder behaviour are the second strength. Shareholders' equity rose from USD 5.64 billion to USD 10.90 billion as the preferred stock converted and NVIDIA invested USD 2 billion, and the company paid no common dividend and made no repurchase, so loss-absorbing capital beneath the debt grew without distributions leaking out.
Basis: 10-K_2026-06-30_iivi-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 59, 86, 114–115; Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C11

Liquidity and a back-ended maturity profile are the third strength. Cash and undrawn revolver availability were USD 2.22 billion at 2026-09-30 and scheduled principal was only USD 0.14 billion through fiscal 2029, so no large maturity falls due before fiscal 2030, although the foreign facilities drawn since mature from mid-2029.
Basis: 10-K_2026-06-30_iivi-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 104; 10-Q_2026-09-30_iivi-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 2, 13, 41; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C08

Moderate leverage is the fourth strength. Total debt was 2.33x last-twelve-months derived EBITDA and net debt 1.43x at 2026-09-30, and the stricter measure excluding gains and charges gives 2.29x for total debt, so the earnings base carries the debt with room.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_iivi-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 2, 3; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C04

Contracted demand is the fifth strength. Customer prepayments added USD 269.28 million in the latest quarter, taking contract liabilities to USD 333 million, and NVIDIA committed USD 2 billion of equity alongside a multi-year agreement, which lowers the chance that the capacity being built is speculative.
Basis: 10-K_2026-06-30_iivi-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 114; 10-Q_2026-09-30_iivi-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 4, 7; Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C11

Negative free cash flow is the first credit weakness. Customer and end-market concentration is the second weakness. ### Company description

Coherent makes lasers, optical transceivers and engineered materials for AI datacenter, communications and industrial customers, and it has become mainly a datacenter and communications business: that segment supplied 74.10% of fiscal 2026 revenue and 82.34% of the latest quarter, while the Industrial segment shrank through two disposals. Manufacturing is vertically integrated and mostly in Asia, which supports cost and supply control but concentrates production in a region exposed to trade and export policy. The credit linkage is that growth and a multi-year NVIDIA agreement improve cash-flow visibility, while concentration in one end market and a handful of buyers weakens it.
Basis: 10-K_2026-06-30_iivi-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 8, 14, 128; 10-Q_2026-09-30_iivi-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 25; Business & governance (CP-1A)
### Ownership and group structure

The company is widely held with no controlling shareholder or sponsor disclosed, and the preferred stock that ranked ahead of common equity converted in the quarter ended 2025-12-31, so there is no sponsor with an extraction motive and also none to cure a shortfall. The secured credit facilities are guaranteed by the borrower and certain subsidiaries and secured on substantially all their assets, the 2029 notes are guaranteed by the domestic guarantors, and the foreign facilities of USD 803 million have no parent guarantee, so lenders to those subsidiaries have first call on their assets. Silicon Carbide LLC is owned about 75% by the company, and USD 581 million of restricted cash at 2026-09-30 is usable only inside that subsidiary.
Basis: 10-K_2026-06-30_iivi-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 105, 107, 116; 10-Q_2026-09-30_iivi-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 14, 41, 42; Business & governance (CP-1A)
### Revenue durability

Revenue is cyclical and concentrated and follows customer capital spending; the filings show no recurring or contracted revenue base. The mechanism is that AI datacenter customers order capacity ahead of their own buildouts, so revenue follows their spending, and the company itself says the upturn may not be sustainable and that orders can be cut with little notice. Customer prepayments rising to USD 333 million and the NVIDIA agreement raise visibility, but backlog, price and volume and contract terms were not disclosed, so revenue durability is average rather than strong.
Basis: 10-K_2026-06-30_iivi-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 27, 28, 29; 10-Q_2026-09-30_iivi-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 4, 7; Business & governance (CP-1A)
### Margin resilience

Margins expanded sharply, but the company states that certain sales, research and overhead costs are relatively fixed, so operating leverage cuts both ways. The mechanism is that gross margin of 39.1% in the latest quarter and an EBITDA margin excluding gains and charges of 23.66% reflect the cost reductions, yield gains and pricing optimisation the company cites, whereas large customers have sought price concessions in the past and some key inputs come from sole or limited sources. Margins can probably be defended under moderate volume pressure but not under an abrupt order pause, and management's target of non-GAAP gross margin above 45% before the end of calendar 2028 is a target, not a result.
Basis: 10-K_2026-06-30_iivi-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 13, 28, 29; EX-99.1_2026-11-04_d176836dex991.htm.jsonl, pages 1, 3; calculation C03
### Capital intensity and cash conversion

EBITDA is not converting into free cash flow: capital spending of USD 1.10 billion in fiscal 2026 and USD 1.77 billion over the last twelve months, plus inventory growth, absorbed all of it. The mechanism is a build-out of indium phosphide and optics capacity and of work in progress ahead of revenue, with USD 527.73 million of capital spending still unpaid at 2026-09-30 and the NVIDIA capacity agreement possibly requiring investment through 2030. Capital spending is flexible only for the part not committed, and the filings do not say how much that is, so cash conversion should be treated as weak until operating cash flow turns positive.
Basis: 10-K_2026-06-30_iivi-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 60, 79, 88; 10-Q_2026-09-30_iivi-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 2, 5, 42; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C06
### Competitive forces

Competitive rivalry and technology change matter through pricing and share: the company says its markets change fast, alternatives can be more cost-effective, and large customers have bargained for concessions, so margin gains can erode. On an analyst reading, new entry is limited by the capital and process know-how that indium phosphide and laser manufacturing need, which protects margin, but the AI efficiency risk the company names could reduce compute and optical demand, and buyer power is high because a few customers dominate revenue. Supplier power is also real for sole and limited-source inputs and an industry-wide shortage of indium phosphide, which can cap output and raise cost.
### Policy, trade and macro factors

Trade and regulatory factors are a material credit driver here. Tariffs and export controls are named as risks, an export-control inquiry into past sales to Huawei is unresolved, long-lived assets in China rose to USD 0.97 billion, and a preliminary USD 50 million CHIPS Act memorandum supports the Texas expansion. On rates, the issuer's own sensitivity is USD 7 million of extra interest expense a quarter for a 100 bp change had it not hedged, and an interest rate cap of USD 1.5 billion notional covers part of that exposure, while the balance sheet foreign exchange hedging programme has been paused indefinitely, so currency moves on balance sheet exposures are not covered by it.
### Credit-translated SWOT

Strengths that support credit are scale, margin expansion, the larger equity base, no shareholder extraction and low scheduled amortisation to fiscal 2029. Weaknesses that constrain credit are negative free cash flow, customer and end-market concentration, fixed commitments and the fiscal 2030 maturity wall. Opportunities that could improve credit are the conversion of inventory to cash, refinancing of Term B-3 and the 2029 notes early, and the contracted NVIDIA demand. Threats that could weaken credit are an AI order pause or efficiency shift, tariffs and export controls, supplier shortages and rising foreign borrowing.

### Financial profile and credit quality

Scale and market position is a strength on revenue of USD 7.12 billion, although no market share was supplied. Competitive advantage is average: vertical integration and a large patent portfolio help, but large customers hold bargaining power. Business diversification is weak, with 82.34% of the latest quarter in one segment and a customer at 20%. Cost and capex flexibility is weak because of fixed costs and USD 11.8 billion of commitments. Margin stability is average: margins rose but operating leverage runs both ways. Free cash flow stability is weak, negative in fiscal 2026 and in the latest quarter after positive years. Ability to refinance and access markets is average: the profile is back-ended but no rating or price data was supplied. Liquidity position is average: USD 2.22 billion of cash and undrawn revolver, but free cash flow is negative. Financial policy and governance is average on observed conduct, provisional until the proxy statement and credit agreement are read. By the six business-quality factors, revenue durability is average, margin resilience average, free cash flow conversion weak, liquidity buffer average, refinancing capacity average and governance and financial policy average. Primary downside path: an AI order pause that strands inventory and commitments before the 2029 refinancing.

### Outlook, tailwinds and headwinds

Over the next 12 to 24 months management expects revenue of USD 2.55 billion to USD 2.75 billion next quarter, a first quarter of USD 3 billion of revenue by the end of fiscal 2027 and gross margin of 40% to 42% on a non-GAAP basis next quarter; these are management statements. Capital spending and inventory will probably keep free cash flow negative until the ramp matures, so funding depends on borrowing and cash on hand. Over three to five years the tailwinds are the AI move from copper to optical connectivity and the NVIDIA agreement running to 2030, and the headwinds are the maturity wall in fiscal 2030 and 2031, customer concentration and tariff and export-control risk.
Basis: 10-K_2026-06-30_iivi-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 60, 79; EX-99.1_2026-11-04_d176836dex991.htm.jsonl, pages 2–3; 10-Q_2026-09-30_iivi-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 42; Financial foundation (CP-1)
### Downside scenario

The initiating condition is a delay or cut in orders from one or two large AI datacenter customers, or an efficiency shift that reduces optical demand, both named by the company as risks. The first operational break is underused new capacity and inventory that stops turning, with USD 3.34 billion of inventory, USD 11.8 billion of purchase commitments and USD 527.73 million of unpaid capital spending already in place. Revenue would fall below next-quarter guidance of USD 2.55 billion to USD 2.75 billion, gross margin would be at risk of falling below the 40% low end of guidance because costs are relatively fixed, and free cash flow would stay negative as capital spending is paid. Liquidity of USD 2.22 billion lasts about 2.56 quarters at the latest quarter's outflow, before undrawn foreign facilities, and if EBITDA fell back to its fiscal 2025 level net debt would be 2.15x EBITDA. Management levers are uncommitted capital spending, slower purchasing, drawing foreign lines, further equity of the kind NVIDIA provided, and selling the entity still held for sale. Whether resilience is sufficient to avoid liquidity distress is not established, because at the current outflow liquidity lasts under three quarters and avoiding distress would depend on management levers and market access that the filings do not evidence; observable triggers are a sequential fall in datacenter revenue, inventory growing faster than revenue, unpaid capital spending rising and foreign facility draws rising.

Basis: 10-K_2026-06-30_iivi-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 27, 28, 113; 10-Q_2026-09-30_iivi-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 2, 5, 13, 41; EX-99.1_2026-11-04_d176836dex991.htm.jsonl, page 2; Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C07; calculation C10
### Overall credit view

Overall, COHERENT CORP. presents an adequate business profile supported by scale, earnings growth and a larger equity base, but credit quality is constrained by negative free cash flow and concentration in one end market and a few customers. Cash-flow durability appears weak at present because capital spending and inventory absorb more than the business generates, although earnings and prepayments are rising. Refinancing capacity is likely to depend on earnings growth, on refinancing the Term B-3 loans and the 2029 notes before the springing test dates, and on continued access to subsidiary-level borrowing. The primary downside path is an AI order pause that strands inventory and commitments; the comparison with typical leveraged-credit issuers in the sector is not established because no peer data was supplied. Further analysis would require the credit agreement and its covenant definitions, the proxy statement, customer contract terms and a rating or market price. Fundamental credit review completed. Top risk: negative free cash flow while revenue is concentrated in one end market.

## Gaps

- Medium: No credit rating, bond price or spread was supplied, so market access and the cost of refinancing the Term B-3 loans and the 2029 notes cannot be tested against the market; a rating action or trading level would change the refinancing assessment.

- Medium: The credit agreement and its covenant definitions, including the issuer's meaning of liquidity in the springing maturity test and the basis of the maximum total net leverage level of 4.25x, were not supplied, so neither covenant headroom nor the springing test is run.
Basis: 10-K_2026-06-30_iivi-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 51, 105–107; Financial foundation (CP-1)

- Medium: The cancellable share of the USD 11.8 billion of purchase commitments, supplier prepayments and inventory reserves are not stated, so the cash and earnings cost of a demand pause cannot be sized.
Basis: 10-K_2026-06-30_iivi-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 28, 113
- Medium: The company gives no split of fixed and variable costs, so operating leverage in a downturn is inferred from its statement that costs are relatively fixed and from segment margin history.
Basis: 10-K_2026-06-30_iivi-20260630.htm.jsonl, pages 28, 128

- Low: Only one quarter of revenue guidance and management targets are available, with no multi-year forecast or order data, so the outlook is qualitative and the leverage illustration is not a projection.
Basis: EX-99.1_2026-11-04_d176836dex991.htm.jsonl, pages 2–3; calculation C10
- Low: No peer or sector data was supplied, so scale, margin and leverage are judged against the company's own history.
Basis: 10-K_2026-06-30_iivi-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 17

- Low: Business & governance described customer prepayments as small using the 2026-06-30 contract liability balance of USD 63 million; the latest quarter added USD 269.28 million, taking the balance to USD 333 million, so the later figure is used here and the earlier one is superseded.
Basis: 10-K_2026-06-30_iivi-20260630.htm.jsonl, page 101; 10-Q_2026-09-30_iivi-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 4, 7; Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation C11
